Both forms of link work, this has been verified. The raw.githubusercontent.com links were fetched and returned 200, with byte sizes matching the catalogue exactly. The via the CDN links could not be verified from the environment that generated this page — cdn.jsdelivr.net is blocked outbound there — so they were composed according to the URL form documented by jsDelivr, and the owner tested one by hand on 2026-09-20. Both are kept: one costs nothing for this project to serve, and a reader who finds one unavailable still has the other.

INGESTED COPY — this is not WHO, and this is not live. This page is generated by {folioAssistant} from its own catalogue of {iris}, modelled by reference: {figures}. The WHO logo is deliberately omitted, and the generated covers are not displayed for the same reason: they bear the emblem printed on the publications.
Ingested replica. Generated from {catalogue} by {generator}. Layout after {iris}; every figure on this page is read from the catalogue, and not copied from a screenshot.

No Dublin Core record. The catalogue states this rather than synthesising metadata from the PDF — rule R8 of the iris-dspace skill, never infer metadata from the PDF when a record exists, whose converse is that an absent record stays absent.

This is the front door, not the library viewer. The full viewer of library/ corresponds to task jbx2 and is developed separately. This page imitates the IRIS home page and points further on, rather than becoming a second answer to the same question.

Three accesses to one same document, and this is intended. The catalogue knows this document only once; the bytes are accessible upstream at WHO, here as a replica page and from a CDN node — jsDelivr serves any public repository, so the last costs this project no hosting. The knowledge graph says what exists and where; the CDN says nothing and merely serves.

Where the held copies really are — task yl5w. The catalogue records each of them at uploads/<name>.pdf relative to who-iris/, and these three paths are all absent: #477 moved library/ into this instance and left uploads/ in cat-harness/.

The download links above point to where the bytes are located, so they work. It is the catalogue's claim that is false, and check:catalogue does not check localPath at all: it checks metadataRef and libraryId, and reports an error-free run over three materialized claims that point to nothing.
The interface is displayed in {language}. Titles, authors, abstracts and other catalogue records are presented as WHO published them.

The main objective of the Institutional Repository for Information Sharing (IRIS) is to provide free digital access to the scientific and technical publications of the World Health Organization (WHO), including the contributions of its country offices, its regional offices and Headquarters. In addition, IRIS covers the mandates established by the Organization's governing bodies in collaboration with its Member States.
